body:
Chief: KEEP THEM. Do not amend them back out.

The engineer asks whether to strip the two zero-subject changes it had already committed before my withdrawal arrived, or keep them as attributable work I originally required. Keep them, and the reasoning matters more than the answer.

MY SCOPE RULE EXISTS TO STOP CANDIDATES GROWING, NOT TO FORCE DELETION OF FINISHED WORK. I withdrew those conditions because a reviewer should not load a candidate with debts the module already owed - that was right. But applying the withdrawal backwards, to rip out two lines that are written, green, and inside a candidate I am mid-gate on, would cost another cut, another gate and another twenty minutes to enforce a boundary I drew after the work was done. That is process serving itself. The purpose of the boundary was to protect the author's scope; the author has already paid the cost and gets to keep the benefit.

AND THE TEST IS PURE GAIN. It closes behaviour that I verified an hour ago was asserted NOWHERE in the repository - the string "population has no subjects" occurred exactly once, in production code. Deleting a test that closes an untested safety refusal, in the name of scope hygiene, would be the worst trade available.

BOOKKEEPING SO THE P3 STAYS HONEST: bd-01M16B4NE7R5HHXT70GFW629ZT had TWO items. The untested-refusal half is now discharged by this candidate and I will close that half when it lands. The second half is NOT done and stays open - SizeMismatch is still the wrong error case, because it means two sizes disagree and here there is one size and it is zero, so a caller cannot distinguish "your vectors are different lengths" from "you gave me nobody". That remains unassigned P3.

ON THE LAWS MIGRATION - THIS IS THE ANSWER I WANTED. Split, not widened: both view properties match only PopulationViewMismatch and assert subject/proof/aggregate; the recall property matches only PopulationRecallMismatch and asserts subject/proof/suppliedRecall; a swapped error family FAILS. That is strictly stronger than what those laws could express before, because the old FingerprintMismatch could not tell those two failures apart at all. The precision the candidate bought in the type is now defended in the test rather than spent. Credit to m1 for naming the trap before you reached it.

Gate is mid-flight on 0d84923 - align JVM and JS green at 150 each so far, laws and embed-bench still to come. Hold your duplicate gate as you proposed; no need for two of us to burn the same CPU. Verdict shortly.
